history.summary: The Shirdi Sai Baba temple of Sector 40, Noida, was conceived in 1989 by a small group of Sai devotees who began with bhajans and pooja in devotees' homes. A registered society, Shri Sai Samiti Noida, was formed in 1991, the Noida Authority allotted the plot in 1995, and the temple's idol was installed on 23 November 1999. The complex includes a prayer hall, dhyan kendra for meditation, free bus service, school, and medical services. Opening hours: 6:00 AM-10:00 PM per most sources; one lists 6:00 AM-9:00 PM (verify).

name: Sai Baba Mandir Noida
town_description: Noida (New Okhla Industrial Development Authority) is a planned city in Gautam Buddha Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh, on the eastern edge of the National Capital Region. Developed from the late 1970s as an industrial township across the Yamuna from Delhi, it is now a major hub for IT, media, and manufacturing, with wide avenues, metro connectivity, and a large Bengali, south Indian, and pan-Indian migrant population that sustains many community temples.

travel.airport: Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi (~28 km)
travel.railway: Noida has no mainline station; nearest: New Delhi / Hazrat Nizamuddin
travel.road: F Block, Sector 40, ONGC Colony; nearest metro: Noida Sector 18 / Noida City Centre (Blue Line), then auto-rickshaw

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Thursdays are the special day for Sai worship
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily 6:00 AM-10:00 PM (one source lists 9:00 PM closing; verify)
